'''Wadi-Wadi''' is an extinct [[Indigenous Australian language]] once spoken in [[Victoria (state)|Victoria]] and [[New South Wales]].

Clark suggests that ''Jari Jari'' is a closely related language,<ref>{{cite book|year=1996 |last=Clark |first=Ian |title=Aboriginal language areas in Victoria: a reconstruction |location=Melbourne |publisher=Victorian Aboriginal Corporation for Languages}}</ref> but this name may refer to other languages.<ref>{{cite book|year=1998 |last1=Blake |first1=Barry |last2=Reid |first2=Julie |chapter=Classifying Victorian languages |title=Wathawurrung and the Colac language of southern Victoria |editor=B. Blake |location=Canberra |publisher=Pacific Linguistics}}</ref><ref>{{cite thesis|type=MA |last=Horgen |first=Michael |year=2004 |title=The languages of the Lower-Murray |publisher=La Trobe University}}</ref>
